statement: Subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $A_i\cap A_j\neq\emptyset$ for all $i,j$. Prove there exist distinct positive integers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ such that for each $j$: $\text{lcm}_{i\in A_j}(x_i) > \text{lcm}_{i\notin A_j}(x_i)$.

Determine the least real $k$ such that $\left(\frac{2a}{a-b}\right)^2+\left(\frac{2b}{b-c}\right)^2+\left(\frac{2c}{c-a}\right)^2+k\geq 4\left(\frac{2a}{a-b}+\frac{2b}{b-c}+\frac{2c}{c-a}\right)$ holds for all real $a,b,c$.

In $\triangle ABC$, $M$ is midpoint of $BC$. Circle $\omega$ inside $\triangle ABC$ is tangent to $AB$, $AC$ at $E$, $F$. Tangents from $M$ to $\omega$ at $P$, $Q$ ($P$ and $B$ same side of $AM$). $X = PM \cap BF$, $Y = QM \cap CE$. If $2PM = BC$, prove $XY$ is tangent to $\omega$.

In $\triangle ABC$ ($\angle A\neq 90^\circ$), $BE$, $CF$ are altitudes. Bisector of $\angle A$ meets $EF$, $BC$ at $M$, $N$. $P$ such that $MP\perp EF$ and $NP\perp BC$. Prove $AP$ passes through the midpoint of $BC$.
Prove that for each $m$, there exist $m$ consecutive positive integers $n$ such that $(1^3+2018^3)(2^3+2018^3)\cdots(n^3+2018^3)$ is not a perfect power.

A graph is divisibility if vertices can be labeled with distinct integers so that edges correspond to divisibility. A graph is permutationary if vertices can be labeled $1,\ldots,n$ and there exists a permutation $\pi$ such that $i$--$j$ iff $i>j$ and $\pi(i)<\pi(j)$. Prove a graph is permutationary iff both it and its complement are divisibility graphs.
Find all $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying: (a) $x+f(y+f(x))=y+f(x+f(y))$ for all $x,y$; (b) the set $\left\{\frac{f(x)-f(y)}{x-y}:x\neq y\right\}$ is an interval.
Mojtaba draws 2018 vectors with zero sum. Players alternate placing vectors end-to-end. The result is a closed polygon; Mojtaba wins if it is non-self-intersecting. Who wins with optimal play?
Let $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$ be an infinite sequence of distinct integers. Prove there are infinitely many primes $p$ for which distinct positive integers $i,j,k$ exist with $p \mid a_ia_ja_k-1$.
A positive integer is useful-but-not-optimized if it is a sum of distinct powers of 3 and powers of 5. Prove infinitely many positive integers are not useful-but-not-optimized.

$\omega$ is the circumcircle of isosceles $\triangle ABC$ ($AB=AC$). $P\in\omega$, $Q\in BC$ with $AP=AQ$. $AP\cap BC=R$. Prove the tangents from $B$ and $C$ to the incircle of $\triangle AQR$ (other than $BC$) meet on $\omega$.

A sequence of $n$ positive integers has at least $2n/3+1$ distinct values, each appearing at most 3 times. Prove there exists a cyclic permutation $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of the sequence with all $n$ sums $b_i+b_{i+1}$ distinct.

Two circles $\omega_1(O)$ and $\omega_2$ intersect at $A$, $B$, with $O\in\omega_2$. $S$ on $AB$ with $OS\perp AB$. $OS$ meets $\omega_2$ at $P$. Bisector of $\widehat{ASP}$ meets $\omega_1$ at $L$ (same side as $A$). $K\in\omega_2$ with $PS=PK$ (same side as $A$). Prove $SL=KL$.
Find the maximum $k$ for which there exist distinct reals $x_1,\ldots,x_k>1$ with $x_i^{\lfloor x_j\rfloor}=x_j^{\lfloor x_i\rfloor}$ for all $i,j$.

$n>1$ and distinct positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_{n+1}$ given. Does there exist $p(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $\leq n$ with: (a) $\gcd(p(a_i),p(a_j))>1$ for all $i\neq j$; (b) $\gcd(p(a_i),p(a_j),p(a_k))=1$ for all distinct $i,j,k$?
Distinct positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ are good if their sum equals the sum of all pairwise gcds. Prove there are infinitely many $n$ with $n$ good numbers.
$2n-1$ distinct positive reals with sum $S$. Prove at least $\binom{2n-2}{n-1}$ ways to choose $n$ of them with sum $\geq S/2$.

Cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ inscribed in $\omega$, $P=AC\cap BD$. $E,F$ on $AB$, $CD$ with $\widehat{APE}=\widehat{DPF}$. Circles $\omega_1$, $\omega_2$ tangent to $\omega$ at $X$, $Y$ and both tangent to circumcircle of $\triangle PEF$ at $P$. Prove $EX/EY=FX/FY$.
